target.title: fix(shared): skip app-group identity migration when OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR is overridden
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit` fails on any Mac where the OpenClaw app previously paired: `GatewayNodeSessionTests` "non bootstrap hello stores primary device token but not additional bootstrap tokens" and "untrusted bootstrap hello does not persist bootstrap handoff tokens" expect `DeviceAuthStore.loadToken` to return nil, but real operator/node device tokens leak into the per-test state dirs. CI (clean machines) passes, so the breakage only hits local development.

Root cause is in prod code, not the tests: `DeviceIdentityStore.loadOrCreate(profile:)` passes `DeviceIdentityPaths.appGroupMigrationSource(profile:)`, which on unentitled processes (test runners, the shipped mac app) points at the machine's real app-group container. Any fresh state dir has no identity file, so `migratedIdentity` copies the machine's real `device.json` and `device-auth.json` — real device tokens included — into every `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-overridden temp dir. That contradicts the function's own contract comment ("only for builds whose store selection fell back to legacy storage"): an explicit override is not the legacy fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `DeviceIdentityPaths.appGroupMigrationSource` now returns nil when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` is set (new `stateDirOverridden` parameter on the injectable variant), honoring the documented legacy-fallback-only contract. Overridden stores (tests, relocated installs) no longer silently import the machine's real pairing identity and tokens.
- `StateDirectoryIsolationTrait` now owns test state-dir isolation instead of only serializing: it pins `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to a fresh temp dir per gated test and afterwards restores the launch value or a run-scoped quarantine dir — never unset — so stray late writes from leaked reconnect tasks cannot reach the developer's real store. The identical 14-line setenv/defer block is deleted from 12 tests; net diff is +76/-191.

## User Impact

- Local `swift test` runs of OpenClawKit pass regardless of machine pairing state, and tests can no longer read or overwrite a developer's real device-auth store (the old behavior could clobber a real node token with a test literal).
- Product behavior change is narrow: unentitled builds running with an explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` override no longer import app-group container identity into the override dir. Default store selection (container/legacy) is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Repro before fix (Mac with real pairing state): both tests fail with the machine's real tokens, `updatedAtMs` matching the app-group container store exactly.
- After fix: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "GatewayNodeSessionTests|DeviceIdentityStoreTests"` passes 44/44 on the same polluted Mac, including the new regression test "provides no app group migration source when the state dir is overridden".
- Full package run: 600 tests / 55 suites green except one unrelated pre-existing flake (`ChatStreamReplayTests` reconnect timeout under full parallel load; passes standalone in 1.5s).
- Real machine stores verified byte-checked after runs: real tokens only, no test literals.
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.5): clean, no actionable findings.
